sections.title: Firm overview
sections.description: A shared comparison layer without flattening the firm-specific operating model.

blocks.title: Legal, KYC, and Ecosystem
paragraphs:
• Copyright: "© 2026 Polyquid" as listed on the landing page.
• Entity Data: No registered legal entity name or jurisdiction is disclosed.
• Compliance: No KYC (Know Your Customer) requirements or geographic restrictions are documented.
• Ecosystem: No native tokens, points systems, or referral programs are currently identified in the sources.

blocks.title: Payout and Trader Compensation
paragraphs:
All mechanics regarding trader compensation are Not Disclosed in the available ledger and rulebook materials. Missing data points include:
• Payout eligibility criteria and withdrawal cadence.
• Profit-share percentages and minimum withdrawal thresholds.
• Payment currency (e.g., USDC, native tokens) and processing timelines.
• Presence or absence of treasury and reserve mechanics.

blocks.title: Execution and Custody
paragraphs:
• Primary Venues: Built on Hyperliquid & Polymarket.
• Primary Technical Ambiguity: There is no disclosure regarding the integration architecture. It is unclear if execution occurs via a centralized sub-account architecture managed by the platform or through direct decentralized wallet connections with the trader.
• Custody/Settlement: Specific wallet permissions, smart-contract components, and settlement paths between the platform and the underlying DEXs are currently undocumented.

blocks.title: Trading Permissions and Restrictions
paragraphs:
The source context provides no documentation or technical specifications for the following categories:
• News Trading: No stated restrictions or permissions.
• Automation/API: No documentation regarding bot integration or API execution limits.
• Copy Trading: No information on mirrored or social trading allowances.
• Prohibited Strategies: No list of banned trading behaviors (e.g., latency arbitrage, hedging across accounts).

blocks.title: Funding Rules and Offers Table
paragraphs: Note: While the "One challenge" program is the primary marketing claim, the underlying financial and risk parameters have not been released for technical review.

blocks.title: Rule Mechanics and Risk Parameters
paragraphs:
Audit of the official source material confirms that no specific risk parameters or performance requirements have been published. The following categories are strictly Not Disclosed:
• Profit targets (percentage-based or absolute).
• Maximum drawdown (trailing, daily, or static).
• Calculation bases for equity or balance-based risk.
• Reset conditions, attempt limits, or breach consequences.

blocks.title: Trader Lifecycle: From Entry to Payout
paragraphs:
• Entry Phase: Public access is limited to "Join the waitlist," "Discord" community entry, and following official "X" channels.
• Evaluation Phase: Platform documentation identifies a singular "One challenge" system as the gateway to the "Every market" claim.
• Post-Evaluation Phases: There is zero documentation regarding the transition from successful challenge completion to funded status.
• Operational Void: Mechanics for capital allocation, risk enforcement protocols, and compensation distribution are not documented. The trader lifecycle currently terminates at the waitlist/community acquisition point.

blocks.title: Project Overview and Operating Model
paragraphs:
• Project Identification: Polyquid is categorized as a "Prop Trading Challenge."
• Current Status: As of the audit date 2026-08-16, the project is in a pre-operational waitlist phase.
• Market Claims: Documentation explicitly states the platform provides access to "Every market" via its "One challenge" model.
• Operational Infrastructure: The project identifies as "Built on Hyperliquid & Polymarket." 
• Operating Model Ambiguity: The specific nature of the trading environment—specifically whether it utilizes simulated paper-trading or live capital—is currently not disclosed in available sources.

blocks.title: Unresolved Questions
paragraphs:
The following material technical and operational questions remain unanswered:
• Cost/Benefit: What are the specific entry costs and profit targets for the "One challenge"?
• Risk Metrics: What are the drawdown limits and the specific mathematical methods used for their calculation?
• Architecture: Is the integration with Hyperliquid and Polymarket via API, or is it a direct smart-contract-based evaluation?
• Legal Standing: Under which jurisdiction does the Polyquid entity operate, and what are the geographic exclusions?
• Payment Rails: What is the specific payout currency and the expected timeframe for settlement?

blocks.title: Conflicts
paragraphs: The sources are consistent but non-substantive. There is a total alignment between the website and the "Rulebook," as both serve solely to broadcast marketing slogans ("One challenge Every market") without providing the underlying operational framework.
